claim: The new diagnostic filter does not drop diagnostics about metadata symbols. When a metadata member has no syntax, the new code (FirstOrDefault()/GetPropertyIdentifierLocation) creates the diagnostic with a null location, which becomes Location.None. In ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource` is then true, so the diagnostic is reported. Example: a referenced generic struct with an unattributed public member makes the consuming project's analyzer report MsgPack004 (an Error per L2) with no location. That contradicts the method's own remarks ('dropped here'), the new README and MsgPack004.md text ('reported by the assembly that defines it'), and L8 (metadata types are not analysed by the consumer). The consumer gets a build-breaking error it cannot fix, not a clean build.

claim: The new filter `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` does not do what its remarks say. A diagnostic built from a metadata member gets a null location, which becomes `Location.None`. `Location.None.IsInSource` is false, so `!diagnostic.Location.IsInSource` is true and the diagnostic is reported. The only diagnostics dropped are those located in another compilation's syntax tree. So once the crash is fixed, a referenced closed generic struct whose public member lacks `[Key]` raises a location-less MsgPack004 Error in the consuming assembly. Ledger L8 says types from a referenced assembly are not analysed by the consumer, so this is a spurious build error, where before the change there was only an AD0001 warning. The same applies to MsgPack003-style `BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull`, which now gets a null location from `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation`.

claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops only diagnostics with an in-source location outside the compilation. Diagnostics with no location (Location.None, which the guarded null-location paths now produce) still pass through. For a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly, MsgPack004 (MemberNeedsKey) is now reported with a null location. Users who previously saw no diagnostic, because the type was skipped, may now get a location-less MsgPack004 error. L2 lists MsgPack004 as an Error, so this could fail builds. L8 says metadata types deliberately get no diagnostics.

Users could lose existing MsgPack0xx warnings or errors without opting in.
